summary:
Sud is a region of Italy and stands under the Italian national framework. No regional statute, court ruling or administrative measure specific to Sud addressing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified, so the assessment for the region rests on documented incidents and on national custody practice as it applies here.

ILGA-Europe's annual country review for Italy, published in February 2025, records a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people in 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly. Among them is a scooter-mounted assault on a young man in Scampia, in the Naples area, in March 2025.

On 13 October 2025 a 63-year-old man was arrested in Torre Annunziata, in the province of Naples, after making stabbing threats against a young LGBTQIA+ activist; local reporting describes it as a grave homophobic episode in the Naples area.

Italy announced in January 2010 that it would open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates, converting an almost empty medium-security prison at Pozzale, near Florence in Tuscany, to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; gay-rights groups welcomed the decision. As of 2013 the facility had not been created, and it remains the only documented Italian special-unit initiative for trans prisoners, announced but never opened. Trans detainees therefore continue to be placed within the ordinary men's and women's prison circuit, including in Sud.
tangentialFactors:
The February 2025 ILGA-Europe review situates the Scampia assault within a national pattern of bias-motivated violence that grew in both volume and geographic spread during 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly across Italy rather than concentrated in any one area.

The Pozzale initiative was a national plan located in Tuscany, not in Sud; its failure to open means no region of Italy has a dedicated trans facility, so the ordinary prison circuit applies uniformly, including for detainees from Sud.
localsOnly:
Residents of Sud are subject to the Italian national legal framework on gender identity and sexual orientation; no region-specific statute of Sud's own was identified in this record.

Trans detainees from the region are held in ordinary men's or women's facilities, as no dedicated transgender prison exists anywhere in Italy following the unimplemented Pozzale plan.
outOfScopeNotes:
No region-specific anti-discrimination statute, court ruling or administrative measure of Sud was located in this inventory; whether Sud has adopted or debated such a measure is unresolved here.

The ILGA-Europe review's characterisation of a 2024 increase in bias-motivated violence is national in scope; the inventory does not break the figure down by region, so Sud's share of that increase is not sourced.

The Torre Annunziata arrest of 13 October 2025 is reported as an arrest; the outcome of any proceedings is not sourced in this inventory.
